summary: Fire tower on Carson Creek Peak near Thunder Bay; a hiking guide dates it to the 1960s, and a 2016 post and a 2025 comment say it still stands.

access.note: Route descriptions start from Boreal Road. No source mentions a closure, gate or permit. Reader comments say visitors climbed the tower, and one comment on the 2009 page says access to the top was restricted unless the first ladder section is reinstalled. Whether the tower can be climbed now is unclear.

notes_for_editor: Build date is only 'put up in the 60's' from one hiking blog (Superior Hiking); no register or heritage record was readable. The brief's firelookout.ca Aldina pages carry no detail (year, height and type all N/A), and the Ontario GeoHub 'tower' dataset page did not render text, so neither is cited. A geocache listing (GC262MF) describes it as built in the '60s and 99 ft tall, but its page did not load, so it is not cited. Height 30.5 m is 100 ft converted; the source says 'about 100 feet'. Status 'standing' rests on a 2016 post and a 2025 reader comment, both informal. The cupola remark from the hiking guide is not explained by any other source. Access 'public' is inferred from route descriptions that mention no closure; confirm before publishing. Top access is unclear: a 2009-page comment says access to the top was restricted unless a ladder section is reinstalled, and a 2025 comment says a cousin climbed to the top. Walking distances conflict: the Superior Hiking guide gives a 4 km round trip (dropped from the story), the 2016 post gives a 3.8 km walk from Boreal Road to the tower, and a reader comment on the 2016 post gives about 5.9 to 6 km one way from the Boreal Road parking spot. The route descriptions differ: the 2009 account turns onto Highway 588 toward Stanley, while the 2016 post takes Highway 11/17 and 590 to Boreal Road. The story gives both routes.
